bindings.label: A man in his 40s presented with a 12-month history of nasal swelling
The swelling gradually increased in size since onset, causing pain and right-sided nasal blockage; no discharge, rhinorrhea, or anosmia were reported.
The nasal swelling caused emotional distress due to its prominent appearance, leading to the patient becoming housebound and experiencing social isolation; medical history included anxiety.

Physical examination revealed a prominent cystic swelling on the right side of the external nose with an associated internal component; the swelling was fluctuant, fluid-filled, and tender, and anterior rhinoscopy showed narrowing of the internal nasal valve.
MRI shows no intracranial connection of the nasal lesion
Histopathology reveals a nasal cyst lined by double-layered epithelium with squamous differentiation and focal corrugated cuticle
Histopathology report states no malignant features or acute inflammatory changes
Benign epithelial cyst of the nasal cavity
